title: Feedback That Changes What People Do
performance: Before giving a colleague feedback, the viewer turns a vague comment into one that names a specific observed behaviour, the effect it actually had, and one concrete next step agreed together, and says it soon after the moment.

audience.assumed_prior: Knows feedback matters; usually gives general praise, general criticism or a hint; has received kind but vague comments themselves.
audience.why: They give feedback to peers or people they lead and want a colleague to actually do something differently.
audience.motivation: Change a colleague's habit without hurting the working relationship.
audience.context: Short corporate video watched at a desk between meetings; expertise reversal applies, so one short worked example and a decision soon.

strategy.name: worked_example_led
strategy.rationale: The skill is rebuilding one comment. One running example (Nina, a team lead, and Theo, whose project updates run long and bury the decision) lets the viewer watch the same comment gain a part at a time, then try a faded version in the check and an independent one in their own week.
strategy.signature_move: Show the vague comment, add the behaviour, add the effect, add one agreed next step, reread the whole comment, then let the viewer rebuild a new one.

misconceptions.belief: A warm, general comment is enough to change what someone does.
misconceptions.why_tempting: It feels kind and the receiver smiles. But it gives a feeling, not a target: nothing says which action to repeat or change (F1, F11).

misconceptions.belief: Naming the trait ('you ramble', 'you're disorganised') is the clearest, most honest feedback.
misconceptions.why_tempting: A label feels like the real point and is quick to say. But it is a conclusion, not the behaviour, and tends to prompt defensiveness with nothing concrete to change (F4, F5).

misconceptions.belief: Being specific means being harsh, so kind feedback has to stay general.
misconceptions.why_tempting: Specific details can feel like an accusation. Specificity is separate from tone: feedback can be specific and warm (F12).

hook.sketch: Imagine Nina, a team lead, after Theo's project update: 'Great job, maybe tighten things up a bit.' Theo smiles, feels fine, and next week runs the update exactly the same way, the decision still buried at the end. On-screen essence: 'Theo felt good. Nothing changed.'

arc.promise: Stay with Nina and Theo, and you will leave able to turn a comment like that into feedback a colleague can actually act on.
arc.bridge_from_prior: You have been Theo: someone said something kind and vague, you felt fine, and you did the same thing again. The intention was good; the comment just gave you nothing to aim at.

sections.goal: the viewer can explain why a kind, vague comment tends to leave what someone does unchanged
concepts: A comment changes behaviour when the person can tell which action to repeat or change (F1)
Feedback does not help automatically just because it was given (F2)
Feedback on the task tends to be more useful than feedback on the person (F3)
sections.recap_after: One line: a feeling moved, behaviour did not.

sections.goal: the viewer can rewrite a vague comment so it names one specific observed behaviour instead of a trait
concepts: Behaviour is what someone could have seen or heard; a label is a conclusion (F4)
Describing what you observed gives the person something to recognise; a trait label tends to prompt defensiveness (F5)
sections.recap_after: The comment now says what Theo did: walked through every workstream before reaching the budget question.

sections.goal: the viewer can complete the comment with the effect it actually had and one concrete next step agreed together
concepts: Name the effect as what actually happened: time ran out, the budget decision slipped a week (F6)
Specific goals beat 'do your best', so end with one concrete thing to try (F7)
Agree the step in conversation so it is owned (F8)
Specific and warm can go together (F12); say it soon, while both remember the details (F9)
sections.recap_after: Reread the whole comment: what he did, what it caused, one step to try. What CHANGES on screen: the single comment gains a part at a time.

sections.goal: the viewer can tell the rewrite that names behaviour, effect and next step from rewrites that miss a part
concepts: Three questions: could someone have seen it? did it really cause that? is there one step to try?
New small moment: a client report arrives on Friday evening and the team checks it over the weekend
sections.recap_after: The answer card shows which part each wrong option missed.

sections.goal: the viewer can use the same three parts to rebuild a real comment they owe this week
concepts: Pick one piece of feedback owed this week, rebuild it, say it soon
Return to Theo: the next update opens with the decision
sections.recap_after: Theo's next update opens with the budget question. What CHANGES on screen: the same meeting, before and after.

arc.payoff: Back to Nina and Theo: the same update, now after the rebuilt comment. Theo opens with the budget question and the team decides it in the room. It answers the hook: this time something concrete changed, not just a feeling. Specific feedback makes change easier; it does not guarantee it.

practice_ladder.description: Nina's comment to Theo rebuilt part by part on screen.
A new small moment; the viewer picks the rewrite that has all three parts.
The viewer rebuilds a real comment they owe this week.

recall_moments.prompt: Nina's comment now says what Theo did. What does it still not tell him?

recall_moments.question: A client report arrives on Friday evening and the team checks it over the weekend. Which comment would you give?
options: A: 'You've been a bit disorganised lately. Try to be more on top of things.'
B: 'The report came in Friday evening, so the team checked it over the weekend. Could we agree a Thursday draft next time?'
C: 'The report came in Friday evening, so the team checked it over the weekend. Please be more careful.'
recall_moments.answer: B names what happened, what it caused, and one step to try, offered as a question to agree.
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: C: it names the behaviour and the effect, so it feels complete, but 'be more careful' is not a step anyone can try. A is a trait label with no behaviour, effect or step.

transfer_tasks.task: Pick one piece of feedback you owe someone this week. Write it as: what they did, what it caused, one thing to try. Check it with the three questions, then say it soon.
transfer_tasks.context: Own job, own colleague, within the week.

gagne.recall_prior: arc.bridge_from_prior (the viewer has had kind, vague comments)
gagne.guidance: strategy.signature_move and the worked example in s2 and s3
gagne.practice: the quiz after s3 and the faded and independent rungs; the s5 task

merrill.problem_centred: One running problem: Nina, Theo and the update comment, in every section
merrill.demonstration: s2 and s3 show the comment gaining a part at a time
merrill.integration: s5 and transfer_tasks[0]: a real comment owed this week

mayer.coherence: one example, one loud thing at a time, no decoration
mayer.signalling: the newly added part of the comment is highlighted at each step
mayer.redundancy: on-screen text is the comment itself; narration adds the why, not a repeat
mayer.contiguity: each new part appears beside the narration that names it
mayer.segmenting: one part of the comment per step in s2 and s3
mayer.pre_training: s1 names the problem before the parts are taught

arcs.attention: hook: a kind comment and no change
arcs.relevance: the viewer's own colleague and feedback owed this week
arcs.confidence: a short worked example, then a three-question test
arcs.satisfaction: the payoff shows the next update going differently

flags: HOOK-NEEDS-FACT: Nina and Theo are invented, framed as 'imagine'; the knowledge sheet gives no real case.
Not verified: the knowledge sheet's attributions were not checked against external sources. Narration says 'tends to' and 'more likely', never 'always'.
Model-neutral: behaviour, effect and next step is presented as one useful structure; SBI (F13, F14) is not named on screen at this length.
DURATION-NOTE: 120 s requested and planned; s1 is the short rest valley.
